rationales.explanation: Charles probes how goal specificity functions in the product experience, including for users with only a general fitness objective.
Charles asks what retention level is required for the service to make economic and business sense.
Charles characterizes the proposed retention level as unusually strong for the category.
Charles tests whether the offering can be unbundled into an app-only or headless subscription for customers who already own rowing equipment.
Charles states that pre-revenue status fits his usual investment focus and explicitly says it is not his concern here.
A packed rowing studio leads Charles to conclude that there is real activity and demand in rowing.
Charles says he likes everything presented, indicating a favorable reaction to the proposed offering.
Charles sees several plausible models and says the company is exploring too many things, creating uncertainty about which business model it will pursue.
Charles expresses a strong personal positive impression of Kevin and Moses.
Charles believes the founders will avoid becoming attached to an approach that does not work, suggesting adaptability.
Charles says he needs clarity on what the core business is, wants a firmer strategic commitment, and does not yet know what the model looks like.
Charles believes the founders could build a product in the rowing category.
